cards.title: See Widely, Think Wisely: Toward Designing a Generative Multi-agent System to Burst Filter Bubbles
cards.relevant_page_map: motivation pp. 1, 5; interface pp. 6–7, 18–19, 24; evaluation pp. 7–14; limitations pp. 14–15.

identity_entries.value: true — page 1 gives the title, authors, venue, year, and DOI.
quotes: "See Widely, Think Wisely: Toward Designing a Generative Multi-agent System to Burst Filter Bubbles" (p. 1)
"In Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’24), May 11–16, 2024, Honolulu, HI, USA." (p. 1)

identity_entries.value: motivation pp. 1, 5; interface pp. 6–7, 18–19, 24; evaluation pp. 7–14; limitations pp. 14–15.
quotes: "We developed a prototype featuring LLM-powered multi-agent characters that users could interact with while reading social media content." (p. 1)
"Our design incorporates multi-agent characters with diverse perspectives generated by state-of-the-art Large Language Model GPT-4." (p. 6)

"Then we evaluated users’ attitude for communicating with AI agents while viewing online posts using our prototype, as well as the effectiveness of LLM-generated opinions on the depth and diversity of users’ information-seeking results, through a user study with experienced social media and online forum users." (p. 7)

"There are three primary limitations in this study: the system’s usefulness awaits further evaluation, the limited scope of the prepared topic, and the limitations of the laboratory study setting." (p. 14)

mechanisms.author_term: LLM-powered Multi-agent Characters — the paper’s label (PDF p. 6).
mechanisms.value: GPT-4 persona agents spanning stakeholder roles and attitudes

mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: This instance defines whose positions are made visible through character backgrounds, avatars, attitudes, and overviews; it does not determine conversational turns, presentation order, progress, or assessment.

This instance defines whose positions are made visible through character backgrounds, avatars, attitudes, and overviews; it does not determine conversational turns, presentation order, progress, or assessment.
Persona backgrounds and distinct positions are visible in the avatar panel and character overview (PDF p. 6), Fig. 3a, Table 1.
quotes: "Our design incorporates multi-agent characters with diverse perspectives generated by state-of-the-art Large Language Model GPT-4." (p. 6)

mechanisms.author_term: Frictionless Interaction Flow — the paper’s label (PDF p. 6).
mechanisms.value: in-post conversational interrogation of persona viewpoints
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA095 Conversational follow-up loop for deeper explanation
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: This instance lets the person question a represented viewpoint and receive a contextual answer; the personae supply the positions, while this dialogue supplies the interrogation workflow.

entries.value: Frictionless Interaction Flow — the paper’s label (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "3.3.2 Frictionless Interaction Flow." (p. 6)

entries.value: in-post conversational interrogation of persona viewpoints
VA095 Conversational follow-up loop for deeper explanation
interrogable perspective dialogue
FC092 perspective-taking and viewpoint framing
This instance lets the person question a represented viewpoint and receive a contextual answer; the personae supply the positions, while this dialogue supplies the interrogation workflow.
The comments-area entrance opens character dialogue during post reading, and GPT-4 answers questions as the exchange develops (PDF pp. 6, 13), Fig. 3b.
quotes: "To ensure a smooth and natural interaction, we integrated the primary entrance to initiate a dialogue with multi-agent characters directly within the comments section of the primary forum-like interface." (p. 6)
"As the conversation developed, users had the opportunity to engage with each character by asking questions, and responses were generated instantly by GPT-4." (p. 13)

mechanisms.author_term: default response options — the paper’s term (PDF p. 6).
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA033 Gallery of generated alternatives to choose among
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: These selectable prompts propose what the person might ask next; they guide inquiry without supplying the character representation, ordering viewpoints, or testing comprehension.

entries.value: default response options — the paper’s term (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Furthermore, we provided default response options generated by LLM during the conversation (Figure 3b)." (p. 6)

entries.value: context-generated follow-up question choices
VA033 Gallery of generated alternatives to choose among
guided conversational inquiry
FC061 inquiry and hypothesis prompting
These selectable prompts propose what the person might ask next; they guide inquiry without supplying the character representation, ordering viewpoints, or testing comprehension.
The choices are generated during conversation, and participants used them to continue inquiry (PDF pp. 6, 11), Fig. 3b.
quotes: "Furthermore, we provided default response options generated by LLM during the conversation (Figure 3b)." (p. 6)

"Since we designed the provided options to be questions that could be asked based on the agent replies, these questions encouraged participants to “further inquire and engage in dialogues” (P5), probably because the options have stimulated participants’ curiosity." (p. 11)

mechanisms.author_term: Progressive Viewpoints Sequence — the paper’s label (PDF p. 6).
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA104 Challenge or counter-position pressed against the person
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: This instance controls when and in what attitudinal order positions appear; it structures exposure independently of the content of each persona or dialogue.

entries.value: Progressive Viewpoints Sequence — the paper’s label (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "3.3.4 Progressive Viewpoints Sequence." (p. 6)

entries.value: similar-to-contrasting staged agent reveal
VA104 Challenge or counter-position pressed against the person
graduated viewpoint sequencing
FC092 perspective-taking and viewpoint framing
This instance controls when and in what attitudinal order positions appear; it structures exposure independently of the content of each persona or dialogue.
Additional agents are revealed incrementally, ordered from viewpoints similar to existing beliefs toward increasingly contrasting ones (PDF pp. 6, 14), Fig. 3d.
quotes: "Each click reveals an additional AI agent along with their opinion, allowing for a more gradual and incremental understanding of the content." (p. 6)

"The progressive role setting, starting from the most similar viewpoint to the original, then gradually introducing more nuanced and diverse perspectives, guided participants from a basic understanding of their existing beliefs to more critical thinking." (p. 14)

mechanisms.author_term: Viewpoints Jigsaw Puzzle — the paper’s label (PDF p. 6).
mechanisms.value: clickable Viewpoints Puzzle indexing agent perspectives
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA031 Navigation index into a long artifact
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: This instance spatially gathers the character viewpoints and provides clickable routes back into their dialogues; its overview/navigation function is distinct from the same display’s illumination reward.

entries.value: Viewpoints Jigsaw Puzzle — the paper’s label (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "3.3.3 Viewpoints Jigsaw Puzzle." (p. 6)

entries.value: clickable Viewpoints Puzzle indexing agent perspectives
VA031 Navigation index into a long artifact
perspective overview and navigation
FC092 perspective-taking and viewpoint framing

This instance spatially gathers the character viewpoints and provides clickable routes back into their dialogues; its overview/navigation function is distinct from the same display’s illumination reward.
Participants used the puzzle as an index, overview, and route into different agent conversations (PDF pp. 10–11), Fig. 5.
quotes: "Several participants utilized the Viewpoints Puzzle as an index, navigating through it to engage in conversations with various AI agents." (p. 10)
"Some participants stated that the Viewpoints Puzzle served as a useful tool for “summarizing and organizing various viewpoints” (P3, P11)." (p. 11)

mechanisms.author_term: “lighting up” the ViewPoints Puzzle — the paper’s term (PDF p. 12).
mechanisms.value: puzzle illumination tied to dialogue and quiz completion
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA059 Progress, coverage or completion tracking
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: This instance externalizes completion state and rewards continued exploration; it neither provides the puzzle’s viewpoint overview nor supplies the questions whose completion changes that state.

entries.value: “lighting up” the ViewPoints Puzzle — the paper’s term (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "They were also motivated to interact through the gamified feature of “lighting up” the ViewPoints Puzzle." (p. 12)

entries.value: puzzle illumination tied to dialogue and quiz completion
VA059 Progress, coverage or completion tracking
gamified exploration progress feedback
FC066 progress and status tracking
This instance externalizes completion state and rewards continued exploration; it neither provides the puzzle’s viewpoint overview nor supplies the questions whose completion changes that state.
Conversation rounds light avatars, while correct viewpoint assessments light puzzle pieces (PDF pp. 6, 12), Fig. 3c, Fig. 3e.
quotes: "When the conversation lasts for five or more rounds, the user is encouraged to explore more viewpoints by “lighting up” other avatars, which consists of five pieces, each representing a different character’s viewpoint." (p. 6)
"Similarly, through answering multiple-choice questions, participants on average lit up 4.33 puzzle pieces of the agents; 11 participants successfully lit up all the puzzle pieces." (p. 12)

mechanisms.author_term: Assessment Task with Multi-choice Qestions — the paper’s label, including its spelling (PDF p. 6).
mechanisms.value_canonical: VA098 Question posed to test or consolidate understanding
mechanisms.what_makes_it_separate: This instance asks the person to discriminate what each agent’s position means; the check is separate from dialogue generation and from the puzzle illumination produced by a correct answer.

entries.value: Assessment Task with Multi-choice Qestions — the paper’s label, including its spelling (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "3.3.5 Assessment Task with Multi-choice Qestions." (p. 6)

entries.value: agent-specific multiple-choice viewpoint checks
VA098 Question posed to test or consolidate understanding
perspective comprehension self-check
FC092 perspective-taking and viewpoint framing
This instance asks the person to discriminate what each agent’s position means; the check is separate from dialogue generation and from the puzzle illumination produced by a correct answer.
Each character receives a viewpoint-specific multiple-choice self-check, and the appendix shows one translated task per agent (PDF pp. 6, 11, 24), Fig. 3e.
quotes: "This task provides users with an opportunity to self-evaluate their understanding of the viewpoints they have interacted with." (p. 6)

"Regarding the multi-choice questions, 13 out of 18 participants rated that these questions facilitated a better understanding of each AI agent’s perspective, while 5 rated neutral (Mean = 3.78, SD = 0.55)." (p. 11)
"Following are examples of the assessment tasks in the Viewpoints Puzzle, one for each AI agent." (p. 24)

entries.value: Through ordinary friends, forum posts, or comments, users might not obtain an immediate response (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "It’s not always convenient to discuss these topics with friends, and if you try to engage through forum posts or comments, there may not be immediate or any responses." (p. 10)

entries.value: Users question an available viewpoint character and receive an immediate generated response while reading the post (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "As the conversation developed, users had the opportunity to engage with each character by asking questions, and responses were generated instantly by GPT-4." (p. 13)

entries.value: M1, M2
author_claim
author_assertion
Users naturally focused on content aligned with prior beliefs, motivating gentler introduction of contrasting views (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "As humans’ natural propensity to focus only on content that aligns with their pre-existing beliefs, it is recommended to introduce them gently to contrasting views." (p. 5)

entries.value: Users begin with one visible opinion and reveal additional agents incrementally from similar toward more contrasting positions (PDF pp. 6, 14).
quotes: "Initially, only one perspective is displayed in the entrance, with the option to expand additional perspectives if the user desires to do so." (p. 6)

"The progressive role setting, starting from the most similar viewpoint to the original, then gradually introducing more nuanced and diverse perspectives, guided participants from a basic understanding of their existing beliefs to more critical thinking." (p. 14)

entries.value: M4
author_claim
author_assertion
The paper characterizes social-media users as unprimed for deep information processing (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "People are typically not primed for deep processing of information on social media; hence, it’s crucial for the system to be engaging." (p. 6)

entries.value: Users navigate among agent dialogues through the puzzle, pursue visible completion, and revisit dialogue while answering viewpoint checks (PDF pp. 10–12).
quotes: "Several participants utilized the Viewpoints Puzzle as an index, navigating through it to engage in conversations with various AI agents." (p. 10)
"In addition, an intriguing behavioral pattern emerged: some participants would click back and forth to review the chat logs while answering the questions." (p. 11)

"Most participants acknowledged a desire to illuminate the ViewPoints Puzzle, with one participant noting that successfully doing so acted as “positive reinforcement that made him feel he have got to know the corresponding agents” (P16)." (p. 12)

entries.value: author_claim
author_assertion

rq3_entries.value: The tool generates and embodies plural viewpoints, proposes follow-up questions, orders exposure, and produces comprehension checks and progress feedback (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Our design incorporates multi-agent characters with diverse perspectives generated by state-of-the-art Large Language Model GPT-4." (p. 6)
"Furthermore, we provided default response options generated by LLM during the conversation (Figure 3b)." (p. 6)

"The progressive role setting, starting from the most similar viewpoint to the original, then gradually introducing more nuanced and diverse perspectives, guided participants from a basic understanding of their existing beliefs to more critical thinking." (p. 14)
"This task provides users with an opportunity to self-evaluate their understanding of the viewpoints they have interacted with." (p. 6)

rq3_entries.value: The person chooses an agent, types or selects questions, evaluates the answers, reconciles positions, and may review dialogue history to answer checks (PDF pp. 10–11).
quotes: "During the conversations, participants could opt to respond either by typing or by selecting from the system-generated options." (p. 10)

"Furthermore, semantic coding of the participants’ responses showed that 12 participants have typed their own opinions, oppositions, or counter-questions to the AI agents, thereby further substantiating the argument that there is a certain level of in-depth thinking during conversations." (p. 10)
"In addition, an intriguing behavioral pattern emerged: some participants would click back and forth to review the chat logs while answering the questions." (p. 11)

rq3_entries.value: not_measured — the study collected immediate ratings, observed use, and interviews after a single viewing task, not retained learning or transfer (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "The experimenters then conducted a semi-structured interview based on the results and observed use patterns." (p. 8)

rq3_entries.value: author_raised — the authors warn that anthropomorphism may produce over-trust and propose intervention when it is detected (PDF p. 15).
quotes: "On the other hand, as continuous interaction [2] and motivation to comprehend an agent’s behavior [81] may enhance users’ tendency of anthropomorphism and result in over-trust towards the agents [20, 37, 65], interventions should be implemented upon detecting signs of over-trust or negligence." (p. 15)

rq3_entries.value: no — support expands through additional revealed viewpoints and does not withdraw as competence grows (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Each click reveals an additional AI agent along with their opinion, allowing for a more gradual and incremental understanding of the content." (p. 6)

rq3_entries.value: Users must continue choosing or composing questions, interpreting positions, and answering assessments; these responsibilities do not change with competence (PDF pp. 10–11).
quotes: "During the conversations, participants could opt to respond either by typing or by selecting from the system-generated options." (p. 10)
"In addition, an intriguing behavioral pattern emerged: some participants would click back and forth to review the chat logs while answering the questions." (p. 11)
"Participants were compensated $25 for an approximately 60-minute session." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: Progressive interaction with assessment tasks could promote thoughtful consideration of diverse viewpoints (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Additionally, progressive interactions with assessment tasks could promote thoughtful consideration." (p. 1)

claim_entries.value: empirical — the prototype was evaluated in a user study (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Then we evaluated users’ attitude for communicating with AI agents while viewing online posts using our prototype, as well as the effectiveness of LLM-generated opinions on the depth and diversity of users’ information-seeking results, through a user study with experienced social media and online forum users." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: single_condition_usability — every participant used the same prototype and then rated and discussed the experience (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Participants were asked to view posts under the topic of “retirement policy” and communicate with AI agents using our system, which was deployed as a web application, on a laptop for around 30 minutes." (p. 8)
"We recruited 18 participants (9 female, 9 male, aged 21-32, referred as P1-P18 hereafter) through word-of-mouth and snowball sampling." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: unspecified — the available token does not preserve that the sample comprised experienced social-media users (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Then we evaluated users’ attitude for communicating with AI agents while viewing online posts using our prototype, as well as the effectiveness of LLM-generated opinions on the depth and diversity of users’ information-seeking results, through a user study with experienced social media and online forum users." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: descriptive_only — results report counts, means, and standard deviations without an inferential comparison (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Table 2: Number of Conversation Rounds and Ratings for Each AI Agent (Mean ± SD)" (p. 10)

claim_entries.value: approximately 60 minutes total, including around 30 minutes with the prototype — (PDF pp. 7–8)
quotes: "Participants were compensated $25 for an approximately 60-minute session." (p. 7)

"Participants were asked to view posts under the topic of “retirement policy” and communicate with AI agents using our system, which was deployed as a web application, on a laptop for around 30 minutes." (p. 8)

claim_entries.value: Agent replies were often broad or vague, and most participants were neutral or negative about being persuaded (PDF pp. 10–11).
quotes: "However, 12 participants pointed out AI agents’ responses often tended to be broad and vague." (p. 10)

"In the post-survey, 7 out of 18 participants indicated that they disagree/strongly disagree with the statement that they could be persuaded by the AI agents (9 rated neutral, 2 rated positive, Mean = 2.61, SD = 0.85)." (p. 11)

claim_entries.value: The single-condition session supports immediate feasibility, engagement, and self-reported reflection, but not a causal claim that the system changes perspectives or breaks filter bubbles; the authors call for controlled comparison (PDF p. 15).
quotes: "Future research could compare participants’ initial opinions before using the system and their post-use opinions, or contrast experiences with and without using the system." (p. 15)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support helps users access and reflect on diverse information during browsing (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Then we evaluated users’ attitude for communicating with AI agents while viewing online posts using our prototype, as well as the effectiveness of LLM-generated opinions on the depth and diversity of users’ information-seeking results, through a user study with experienced social media and online forum users." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: unspecified — no novice, learner, professional, or expert role governs use.
knowledge_or_concept_gap — filter-bubble exposure narrows the viewpoints available for users to understand and consider (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "The proliferation of AI-powered search and recommendation systems has accelerated the formation of “filter bubbles” that reinforce people’s biases and narrow their perspectives." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study analyzed behavior, engagement, information diversity, and depth of processing (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "In the end, we arrived at four themes: overall user behavioral patterns, engagement, diverse information, and in-depth information processing." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the system orders exposure from similar toward contrasting positions (PDF p. 14).
quotes: "The progressive role setting, starting from the most similar viewpoint to the original, then gradually introducing more nuanced and diverse perspectives, guided participants from a basic understanding of their existing beliefs to more critical thinking." (p. 14)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — the design deliberately brings users into contact with viewpoints that challenge their beliefs (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "As a result, it is imperative that we utilize design to encourage users to interact with perspectives that challenges their own beliefs." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — the dialogue generates a new response as the person questions each character (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "As the conversation developed, users had the opportunity to engage with each character by asking questions, and responses were generated instantly by GPT-4." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_or_foundation_model — GPT-4 generates the characters and viewpoints (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "Our design incorporates multi-agent characters with diverse perspectives generated by state-of-the-art Large Language Model GPT-4." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the meaning-bearing support is generated by GPT-4 (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "We developed a prototype featuring LLM-powered multi-agent characters that users could interact with while reading social media content." (p. 1)

"Third, we conducted the evaluative study in a laboratory setting, where participants were required to complete tasks independently within a limited timeframe." (PDF p. 15)

cards.notes: - The participants are experienced general online-content consumers rather than practitioners, students, crowdworkers, or researchers. `participant_type` has no general-public/consumer value, so `unspecified` loses the sample’s alignment with the intended audience.
